# ISSUE-28 implementation plan

Extend the existing post-Episode 000 DEEP FIELD connection with message boards, threads, People, Directory, local history, and a clue-led hidden command. Keep the legacy Messages list and the reviewed door host available from the signed-in menu. Use the same local save and settings for BBS progress and presentation.

## Dimensions and budget

The WorkUnit sets size to `multi_area` and the compiled profile to `detailed`. Advisory assessment for the unspecified dimensions is known uncertainty and standard risk. Allow roughly 8–14 engineering hours plus 1–2 hours for review, verification, and rework. The two pure layers, browser integration, and CI evidence fit within the approved 32-hour claim budget. See `.swarm/active/WORKUNIT.md:9` and the compiled lease instructions.

## What we know

- The hub calls `getBbsOffer` with current facts, and the offer loads the first eligible endpoint and its flat, numbered Messages list. DEEP FIELD requires `completed:episode.000`. The exact banner and farewell are established story content. `src/main.ts:110`, `src/bbs/bbs.ts:14`, `content/bbs/deep-field.json:2`, `docs/game-design.md:96`, `docs/game-design.md:108`.
- The current BBS JSON parser knows two record kinds. Archive records already have board, sender, date, and search metadata. Community packages are flattened with inherited credit before reference validation. Node and browser discover the same JSON tree, and Vite rejects shared validator errors. `src/content/schema.ts:129`, `src/content/validate.ts:49`, `src/content/validate.ts:118`, `src/content/validate.ts:243`, `src/content/node.ts:5`, `src/content/browser.ts:3`, `scripts/content-plugin.ts:11`.
- BBS reads write namespaced keys to `bbsReadMessages`. Archive reads separately grant `read:<id>` into `archives`, which Episode 000 uses. Archive search hides `searchOnly` records except on exact keyword matches. `src/main.ts:126`, `src/progress/save.ts:218`, `src/app/tools.ts:101`, `src/world/archive.ts:9`, `tests/unit/episode.test.ts:118`.
- The door host lists available registered doors over current facts and saves checkpoints and rewards together. The BBS wrapper owns routing, blocks commands during async launch, and restores the signed-in menu after exit or failure. `src/doors/registry.ts:26`, `src/doors/host.ts:42`, `src/doors/host.ts:70`, `src/bbs/door-session.ts:15`, `src/bbs/door-session.ts:39`.
- The browser starts a localStorage-backed v2 save session and includes support for v0 and v1 migration and future-version write refusal. Settings are applied at startup and on change. The terminal already uses native buttons and a command form. Its CRT overlays currently sit above the text. `src/main.ts:28`, `src/main.ts:38`, `src/main.ts:78`, `src/progress/save.ts:141`, `src/progress/save.ts:184`, `src/terminal/terminal.ts:37`, `src/terminal/terminal.ts:92`, `src/style.css:75`.
- Sector visibility and enterability are pure queries of existing facts. The map's enter handler carries progression side effects. The directory can read listings without invoking that handler. `src/world/map.ts:9`, `src/app/tools.ts:113`.

## What we're assuming

- One connection endpoint with two in-board message boards is enough to demonstrate board navigation. Keep `deep-field` as the endpoint, and confirm in the production content test that both boards appear after the same existing completion gate.
- A single authored choice per thread with a visible, reloadable local response satisfies the persisted consequence. Test both options on separate saves, and repeat with the selected and unselected IDs on the same save.
- Three BBS-scoped palettes (Amber, ANSI, and High Readability) satisfy the theme requirement. Use the same preference control in the hub and BBS settings and check both the token matrix and the running UI. The implementation should use the colors in the tested source for rendering.
- The compiled base includes the door host required by the issue dependency. This was checked against the supplied source snapshot and its door tests. The operator's Git commit identity is unavailable in the snapshot, as described in `.swarm/prompts/developer.md:22`.

## Open questions

- Actual computed contrast, keyboard focus, overlay visibility, and short-viewport scrolling require the implemented DOM. Step 5 specifies the surfaces and focus behavior. Step 6 and the existing Linux Chromium job close the runtime checks. The planner's browser capability is unavailable, and local validation Chromium is unsupported per `.swarm/rules/lessons.md:10`.
- Browser engines other than the configured Chromium project, live Pages mode, and other SwarmOS harness/backend or OS combinations are outside the configured execution paths. The local evidence targets isolated native Codex on Linux under Node 24, and the external UI evidence targets GitHub Actions Chromium on Ubuntu. `.swarm/config.yaml:4`, `.swarm/config.yaml:16`, `.swarm/config.yaml:59`, `playwright.config.ts:5`, `.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:11`.

## Implementation sequence

The flat list and the richer message boards can share a connection without sharing their navigation state. The BBS model should resolve content and report local effects, the scene should render them, and the app should apply them through the save session. This keeps Node tests on the same command path the browser uses.

1. **Define and validate the BBS records.** In `src/content/schema.ts`, extend `archiveSchema` and `bbsMessageSchema` with `origin: fictional | reviewed-community` defaulting to `fictional` and message presentation independent of origin. Default archives to recovered and BBS posts to historical. Use explicit authored presentation such as AI fictional or private where appropriate. Add `bbsMessageBoardSchema` (`kind: message-board`, `id`, endpoint `bbs`, `title`, `description`), `bbsThreadSchema` (`board`, `title`, nonnegative `order`, ordered `messages`, authored `replies`), `bbsProfileSchema` (`bbs`, `characterId`, `handle`, `bio`), `bbsSecretSchema` (`bbs`, single command token, `clueMessageId`, output), and `bbsInterfaceSchema` for interface copy. Thread message references use tagged `{ kind, id }` pairs for BBS posts and archives. Each reply has an ID unique to its thread, a label, and a `messageId` pointing to a BBS response record on the same message board. Allow BBS posts to name the existing endpoint or a message board. Add the kinds and types to `Content.bbs` and the dispatch union in `src/content/validate.ts`. Validate against kind-specific ID sets and report exact nested fields such as `messages.0.id`, `replies.0.messageId`, and `characterId`. Reject cross-board BBS references, reply targets already public as base posts, duplicate choice IDs, reserved/duplicate command tokens, and clues that lack a public thread route on the same endpoint. Archive references resolve after community flattening and honor both `requires` and `searchOnly`; explicitly reject search-only archive references in new threads. Retain existing archive schema defaults, condition checks, and manifest shape. Step output is a validated reference graph with actionable errors at the source file and field.

2. **Implement the signed-in BBS model and authored examples.** In `src/bbs/bbs.ts`, keep `getBbsOffer` as the connection lookup and expand it to supply child boards, threads, profiles, secrets, and sector records to `createBbs`. Keep `MESSAGES` and its ordered `READ <number>` route as the legacy endpoint list. Add `BOARDS` → `BOARD <id>` → `THREAD <id>`, `REPLY <id>` in an open thread, `PEOPLE` → `PROFILE <id>`, `DIRECTORY` → `DOORS` or `NETWORK`, and `HISTORY`. Provide contextual Back and Main Menu routes, and share command dispatch between on-screen actions and typed input. Sort threads by authored order then ID, and render base messages in reference-array order with authored sender and date. Filter current visibility at listing and opening, and omit a thread with no visible base message. Append the selected authored response to the opened thread and mark the choice selected on later opens. Use `mapNodes` over current facts for an informational network listing, displaying a restricted marker for visible locked sectors. Keep sector details that require entry within the existing map path. Maintain `DOORS` as a direct main-menu action using the existing registry, and keep its gate and return behavior. Dispatch secrets only after sign-in, case-insensitively and with exact valid arity, outside the help/action lists.

   Add `content/bbs/general.json` and `content/bbs/second-line.json` as the two message boards, `content/bbs/relay-thread.json` for a short ECHO note and two replies, and `content/bbs/second-line-thread.json` for the existing gated community archive item. Put the root and two scripted results in `content/bbs/relay-note.json`, `content/bbs/relay-receipt.json`, and `content/bbs/relay-deferred.json`. Give the public root note a legible command clue. Add `content/bbs/echo-profile.json` pointing to the existing ECHO character and `content/bbs/linecheck.json` for the optional local discovery. Keep the hidden result independent of episode facts, doors, and ordinary navigation. Mark the existing credited archive in `content/community/first-light.json` as reviewed and mark `content/archives/lore-last-sysop.json` as historical so the legacy read retains its presentation. Use `content/bbs/interface.json` for UI labels, help, history display text, and message badges, with `src/bbs/copy.ts` exporting the bundled JSON copy and formatting named placeholders. Validate it through the shared JSON loader. Keep the original banner and greetings in `content/bbs/deep-field.json`. Step output is a data-driven, signed-in command surface whose examples require only bundled content.

3. **Persist actual local progress and history.** In `src/progress/save.ts`, add a defaulted `bbs` object for first reply per thread, discovered secret IDs, and an ordered list of typed action records. Keep v2 and `bbsReadMessages`, and populate defaults in `freshSave` and the v0/v1 migration. Recover missing or malformed new fields locally so the original progress and door slots still load. Use stable fact-independent content IDs. Add `BbsSnapshot`, `BbsEffect`, and `applyBbsEffect` in `src/bbs/progress.ts`. Read the latest snapshot at dispatch and emit a composable delta so a successful reply or first discovery and its history entry share one save write. Use the existing namespaced BBS read keys for any displayed messages that acquire read markers. If a saved selection references removed content, keep History readable and offer the current authored choices. Use the current same-tab in-memory fallback when a save write refuses, with JSON feedback if the scene stays open after a persistence failure. Respect the future-save guard. Ordinary actions log only successful local sign-in, board/thread/profile entry, legacy message read, directory views, successful door launch, authored reply, first hidden discovery, and signed-in disconnect. Record actions on explicit dispatch. Keep a bounded newest 100 entries in insertion order, display oldest to newest, and store only action kind and applicable content IDs. Use a neutral fallback for missing references. Keep raw input, typed handles, arbitrary prose, timestamps, and visitor metrics outside the history model.

   Update `createBbsDoorSession` in `src/bbs/door-session.ts` to preserve the launch guard, pass live facts and save snapshots to the BBS, and emit a history effect only after a successful launch. Update the BBS connect branch in `src/main.ts` to supply the live snapshot, apply effects, and call `session.persist` once per BBS action with a save effect. Keep door checkpoints/rewards owned by the existing host. Step output is a history and choice round trip through `openSaveSession` with legacy progress and unsupported saves intact.

4. **Wire terminal presentation and navigation.** In `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts`, render grouped output blocks in order. Supply JSON labels and semantic classes for system, human historical, AI-authored fictional, recovered archive, private, door, network error, and restricted content. Keep the existing `.system`, `.history`, and `.sysop` hooks where applicable. Use visible origin labels and a distinct reviewed badge with inherited credit when available. In `src/bbs/door-session.ts`, route screens with door presentation, lifecycle failures with network-error presentation, and unavailable doors with restricted presentation. Extend `Terminal.print` in `src/terminal/terminal.ts` for grouped BBS tones using the existing text-node and live log model. In `src/world/archive-view.ts`, add the same origin distinction to the opened archive record alongside the existing credit; preserve search, reader focus, metadata, and the `onRead` callback. New buttons use explicit commands as keys and native activation. Give opaque authored action labels no typed-command precedence. Return focus to the prompt after navigation and close, direct focus to the settings control when opening it, and preserve the handle-form and door focus paths. Step output is one keyboard and pointer route to every visible feature, with origin and output type understandable without color.

5. **Apply a testable theme preference.** Add pure `src/bbs/themes.ts` exports for theme IDs and opaque palette values, and use its IDs in the defaulted `preferences.bbsTheme` schema. In `src/app/settings.ts`, add a labelled native theme select using JSON names and pass the theme through `applyPreferences`. In `src/main.ts`, reuse the existing settings panel callbacks for hub and signed-in BBS Settings, apply the theme tokens on startup and change, and leave mute, effects, reduced motion, and reset routed through the same preferences. Close the BBS settings panel on close or navigation with prompt focus restored. In `src/style.css`, scope the BBS palette to the BBS. Route actual BBS backgrounds and text colors through the tested tokens for the log, each output tone and origin badge, controls, settings, prompt, dim hints, and hover/focus states. Put the existing CRT effects below opaque BBS text surfaces with a visible outer gutter, and keep the effects and reduced-motion selectors effective. Use generous spacing and no text glow in High Readability. Step output is a live palette change with persisted selection and a clear foreground/background pair for every BBS text state.

6. **Verify focused behavior and hand off browser evidence.** Extend the unit suites and existing Chromium journeys identified below. Include one mixed-input journey through boards, thread, reply, profile, directory, history, and theme, plus reload assertions for choice and history. Cover tab/Enter and button activation, and use the clue to type the hidden command. Use the existing production-build fixture and CI job. Verify every contract criterion against TEST_PLAN.md and record results on the actual candidate. Keep Chapter 2 plot advancement, access levels, and events outside this feature.

# ISSUE-28 test plan

The acceptance rows follow the order in `.swarm/active/WORKUNIT.md:28`. Verify the implemented behavior on the candidate source. The runtime and role assignments below distinguish Node evidence, source review, and the Chromium job.

## Acceptance coverage

| # | WorkUnit criterion | Cases and verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Unit tests cover board listing, thread order, opening a thread, choosing an authored reply and its persisted consequence, viewing a profile, and listing the directory | **D1**, `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts`. Before completion, DEEP FIELD is absent. After completion, sign in and list both boards. Use fixture records in shuffled input order and with equal thread order to assert the ID tie-break; check base message display follows authored reference order and preserves sender/date. Open a thread and confirm its allowed actions and output. Reject invalid IDs, extra input and wrong phases. Select each authored reply on separate saves. Check the chosen response appears once, reopening the thread shows the same choice, and a second selection on that save produces no effect. Persist and construct a fresh session from storage to verify the visible response and choice. View the authored fictional character profile and exercise Back. List doors from the existing host and sectors through the network directory. Check available, restricted, and invisible sector cases, and compare the available door list against the host. Verify the listings grant no facts, do not open a real connection, and do not launch a door by listing it. |
| 2 | Session history records real local actions only, persists across reloads, and contains no invented visitors or statistics | **D1**, `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts` and `tests/unit/save.test.ts`. Drive the actual dispatcher and apply its effects through `applyBbsEffect` over `openSaveSession` with memory storage. Compare the exact empty log, then the exact ordered entries after known successful local actions, including a successful door launch via the wrapper. Interleave auto-connect, invalid commands, HELP, failed door launch, and HISTORY views and assert the ordered log stays exact. Check stable IDs, bounded retention at the newest 100, and the neutral label for a removed ID. Assert raw custom handles, invalid input, visitor fields and statistics are absent from stored history and its rendered lines. Reopen from the same storage, observe earlier actions, and verify old saves start empty. Exercise write refusal and confirm in-memory feedback plus future save byte preservation. **B1** reloads the real UI and verifies reply and locally observed history. |
| 3 | A hidden command fixture shows that the command works without appearing in help, and that its discovery persists | **D1**, `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts` and `tests/fixtures/bbs-discovery.json`. Load a fixture with a public authored thread note and optional secret. Confirm the command is absent from rendered action descriptors and HELP across ordinary signed-in screens, before and after discovery, while the clue is readable in the thread. Reject malformed or pre-sign-in use. Dispatch the clue's exact command in mixed case, assert the authored output and one discovery/history record, save/reopen and verify that command discovery remains present with a repeated invocation adding neither a discovery nor a duplicate history event. Repeat the clue reachability check on real bundled content. **B1** follows the bundled clue and checks that the previous discovery survives reload. |
| 4 | Content validation rejects a thread or reply pointing at an unknown message, and a profile pointing at an unknown character | **D1**, `tests/unit/content.test.ts`. Pass one valid graph into `loadContent`, then mutate each reference independently into a missing ID and a wrong-kind existing ID where applicable. Assert the source path and `messages.0.id`, `replies.0.messageId`, or `characterId` diagnostic. Include same-board validation, repeated reply IDs, search-only archive rejection, missing public clue and secret command collision cases. Check bundled archive provenance default and explicit reviewed credit after flattening, plus backward-compatible archive shapes and messages pointing to an endpoint. Use existing CLI/build validation entry-point tests to establish shared rejection behavior. **D2** validates the authored production JSON and reports `Content OK`. |
| 5 | Theme choice persists, every theme meets WCAG AA text contrast by a unit test of its colour values, and the effects and reduced-motion settings still apply | **D1**, `tests/unit/settings.test.ts` and `tests/unit/save.test.ts`. Import the actual selectable theme table and compare every active text pair for the three themes at a 4.5:1 minimum. Use WCAG sRGB linearization and relative luminance. Enumerate all actual pairs for normal and dim log/command text, all eight output categories, both origin badge styles, control text, and rest/hover/focus/select/prompt backgrounds. Assert the focus outline has at least 3:1 against adjacent surfaces. Check preference startup/default, invalid theme fallback, one round trip for every theme and simultaneous motion/effects values, and existing automatic-vs-explicit motion behavior. **B1**, `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` and `tests/e2e/settings.spec.ts`, changes the theme, checks actual computed text/background on representative message and control elements, reloads, and confirms the selected option and appearance. Exercise the high-readability palette with effects on and off, and browser reduced motion and persisted explicit motion. Check that the decorative layers remain below BBS text. |
| 6 | All new navigation works by keyboard and pointer, and a browser test in the `Browser tests` workflow reads a thread, replies, opens a profile and changes theme | **D3** types the updated specs and the tester independently reviews the native controls and configured discovery. **B1**, `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts`, drives the production bundle in Chromium. Join with the completed-save fixture. Use one keyboard-led and one pointer-led route or parameterize the same route for both. Reach Boards, choose board and thread, read authored content, select a reply, visit People and open a profile, reach both Directory branches and History, and change theme with the native control. Include at least one Tab/Enter menu activation and a typed public command. Verify accessible names, selected state, prompt focus after transitions and Settings close, and visible Back and Main Menu links or buttons. In the keyboard route use real focus movement to reach the features. Exercise control visibility and focus in a narrow viewport. Check the legacy login, Messages, door return, and Episode 000 journey with the existing browser specs. |

B1 preserves the pre- and post-completion journeys and door behavior. Inspect BBS data access for local-only save and bundled JSON, no free-text posting, no new network calls, and a discoverable-only optional secret with no puzzle or door dependency. Preserve authored historical dates and counts in their existing story context, outside local history. `tests/unit/episode.test.ts:118`, `tests/unit/episode.test.ts:232`, `tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts:32`, `docs/game-design.md:96`.
